+# Robustness of ancilla-free testers
+
+## Abstract
+
+Ancilla-free testers with a common normalization state have the robustness of their canonical POVMs.
+
+**Definition 1.1 (Quantum testers).**
+
+$$\forall (y: \operatorname{Type}), (\forall (x: \operatorname{Type}), (\forall (j: \operatorname{Type}), ([\operatorname{Fintype}\left(y\right)], ([\operatorname{DecidableEq}\left(y\right)], ([\operatorname{Fintype}\left(x\right)], ([\operatorname{Fintype}\left(j\right)], (\forall (t: (j) \to (\operatorname{Matrix}\left((y \times x), (y \times x), \mathbb{C}\right))), ((\operatorname{D5.S3.Quantum.QuantumChannels.AncillaFreeTesterRobustnessEquality.IsTester}\left(t\right)) \Leftrightarrow ((\forall (a: j), (\operatorname{Matrix.PosSemidef}\left(t\left(a\right)\right))) \land (\exists (\sigma: \operatorname{Matrix}\left(x, x, \mathbb{C}\right)), ((\operatorname{D5.S3.Quantum.Information.SLDSpectralEnergy.IsDensity}\left(\sigma\right)) \land (\sum_{a: j} (t\left(a\right)) = \operatorname{Matrix.kronecker}\left((1: \operatorname{Matrix}\left(y, y, \mathbb{C}\right)), \sigma\right)))))))))))))$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Quantum/QuantumChannels/AncillaFreeTesterRobustnessEquality.IsTester` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Citation.* Michal Sedlák; Daniel Reitzner; Giulio Chiribella; Mário Ziman (2016). *Incompatible measurements on quantum causal networks*. DOI: [10.1103/PhysRevA.93.052323](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevA.93.052323). URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/1511.00976v2>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+A tester is a finite family t of positive semidefinite effects on the output-input tensor product. Its sum is the output identity tensored with a density matrix σ on the input. Here IsDensity means positive semidefinite with complex trace equal to one. This is the tester definition in ti_pra_07.tex, lines 247–259.
+
+**Definition 1.2 (Compatibility after adding tester noise).**
+
+$$\forall (y: \operatorname{Type}), (\forall (x: \operatorname{Type}), (\forall (j: \operatorname{Type}), (\forall (k: \operatorname{Type}), ([\operatorname{Fintype}\left(y\right)], ([\operatorname{DecidableEq}\left(y\right)], ([\operatorname{Fintype}\left(x\right)], ([\operatorname{Fintype}\left(j\right)], ([\operatorname{Fintype}\left(k\right)], (\forall (lam: \mathbb{R}), (\forall (a: (j) \to (\operatorname{Matrix}\left((y \times x), (y \times x), \mathbb{C}\right))), (\forall (b: (k) \to (\operatorname{Matrix}\left((y \times x), (y \times x), \mathbb{C}\right))), ((\operatorname{D5.S3.Quantum.QuantumChannels.AncillaFreeTesterRobustnessEquality.TesterCompatibleAt}\left(lam, a, b\right)) \Leftrightarrow (\exists (e: (j) \to (\operatorname{Matrix}\left((y \times x), (y \times x), \mathbb{C}\right))), (\exists (f: (k) \to (\operatorname{Matrix}\left((y \times x), (y \times x), \mathbb{C}\right))), (\exists (c: ((j \times k)) \to (\operatorname{Matrix}\left((y \times x), (y \times x), \mathbb{C}\right))), ((\operatorname{D5.S3.Quantum.QuantumChannels.AncillaFreeTesterRobustnessEquality.IsTester}\left(e\right)) \land ((\operatorname{D5.S3.Quantum.QuantumChannels.AncillaFreeTesterRobustnessEquality.IsTester}\left(f\right)) \land ((\operatorname{D5.S3.Quantum.QuantumChannels.AncillaFreeTesterRobustnessEquality.IsTester}\left(c\right)) \land ((\forall (u: j), (\sum_{v: k} (c\left((u, v)\right)) = \operatorname{HSMul.hSMul}\left((1: \mathbb{R}) - lam, a\left(u\right)\right) + \operatorname{HSMul.hSMul}\left(lam, e\left(u\right)\right))) \land (\forall (v: k), (\sum_{u: j} (c\left((u, v)\right)) = \operatorname{HSMul.hSMul}\left((1: \mathbb{R}) - lam, b\left(v\right)\right) + \operatorname{HSMul.hSMul}\left(lam, f\left(v\right)\right))))))))))))))))))))))$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Quantum/QuantumChannels/AncillaFreeTesterRobustnessEquality.TesterCompatibleAt` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Citation.* Michal Sedlák; Daniel Reitzner; Giulio Chiribella; Mário Ziman (2016). *Incompatible measurements on quantum causal networks*. DOI: [10.1103/PhysRevA.93.052323](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevA.93.052323). URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/1511.00976v2>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+The noise testers e and f have the outcome types of a and b. A joint tester c has outcomes j × k, and its marginals are the two mixtures at the same real weight lam. The three testers may have different normalization states, and the noise need not be ancilla-free. The predicate itself allows every real lam; robustness restricts lam to the unit interval. These are the marginal and noise conditions in ti_pra_07.tex, lines 451–459 and 567–570.
+
+**Definition 1.3 (Tester robustness).**
+
+$$\forall (y: \operatorname{Type}), (\forall (x: \operatorname{Type}), (\forall (j: \operatorname{Type}), (\forall (k: \operatorname{Type}), ([\operatorname{Fintype}\left(y\right)], ([\operatorname{DecidableEq}\left(y\right)], ([\operatorname{Fintype}\left(x\right)], ([\operatorname{Fintype}\left(j\right)], ([\operatorname{Fintype}\left(k\right)], (\forall (a: (j) \to (\operatorname{Matrix}\left((y \times x), (y \times x), \mathbb{C}\right))), (\forall (b: (k) \to (\operatorname{Matrix}\left((y \times x), (y \times x), \mathbb{C}\right))), ((\operatorname{D5.S3.Quantum.QuantumChannels.AncillaFreeTesterRobustnessEquality.testerRobustness}\left(a, b\right): \mathbb{R}) = \operatorname{sInf}\left(\{(lam: \mathbb{R}) \mid ((0: \mathbb{R}) \le lam) \land ((lam \le (1: \mathbb{R})) \land (\operatorname{D5.S3.Quantum.QuantumChannels.AncillaFreeTesterRobustnessEquality.TesterCompatibleAt}\left(lam, a, b\right)))\}\right))))))))))))$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Quantum/QuantumChannels/AncillaFreeTesterRobustnessEquality.testerRobustness` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Citation.* Michal Sedlák; Daniel Reitzner; Giulio Chiribella; Mário Ziman (2016). *Incompatible measurements on quantum causal networks*. DOI: [10.1103/PhysRevA.93.052323](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevA.93.052323). URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/1511.00976v2>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Tester robustness is the infimum of the real weights in the closed unit interval for which separate tester noises give compatible mixtures. The source uses a minimum in ti_pra_07.tex, lines 574–577; this infimum formulation makes no assertion of attainment.
+
+**Definition 1.4 (Compatibility after adding measurement noise).**
+

+
+The families u, v and g are POVMs: every effect is positive semidefinite and each whole family sums to the identity. The measurement noise condition is stated in ti_pra_07.tex, lines 761–765.

+*Commentary.*
+
+First, tensoring each effect of a POVM with ρ gives a tester: Kronecker products preserve positive semidefiniteness, and the effects sum to I ⊗ ρ. Conversely, take the partial trace over x of each tester effect. This preserves positive semidefiniteness and finite sums. A tester normalized by any density matrix σ is sent to a POVM because the partial trace of I ⊗ σ is (tr σ)I = I.
+
+For a fixed lam, suppose u, v and g are noise and joint POVMs for m and n. Tensor all three families with ρ. Distributing the Kronecker product over the marginal sums, addition and real scalar multiplication gives noise and joint testers for m ⊗ ρ and n ⊗ ρ. In the reverse direction, start with arbitrary noise testers e and f and a joint tester c. Apply the partial trace over x to all three families and their marginal equations. They become POVMs, and tr ρ = 1 sends m(a) ⊗ ρ to m(a) and n(b) ⊗ ρ to n(b). Thus compatibility at lam is equivalent for the product testers and the output POVMs, even when e, f and c have different normalization states.
+
+Next tensor noise and joint POVMs with the identity on Fin r. Positivity, unit normalization and the marginal equations are preserved. For the reverse direction assume 0 < r and compress every effect to the principal submatrix indexed by pairs (b,0). Principal submatrices preserve positivity. The inclusion b ↦ (b,0) is injective, so compression preserves the identity, and it commutes with finite sums, addition and real scalar multiplication. The compressed entries of t ⊗ I are exactly the entries of t. Consequently compression turns noise and joint POVMs on y × Fin r into noise and joint POVMs on y with the required marginals.
+
+The trace equation tr ρ = 1 implies ρ ≠ 0, hence some column has a nonzero entry. The span of the columns therefore has positive dimension, giving 0 < rank ρ. The first pair of implications identifies the feasible weights in [0,1] for the product testers with those for m and n. The tensor and compression implications identify the latter set with the feasible weights for the canonical POVMs when r = rank ρ. Composing these set equalities and taking infima proves the displayed equality. No minimizer or numerical robustness value is needed.

+    [Fintype x] [Fintype j] [Fintype k]
+    (a : j → Matrix (y × x) (y × x) ℂ) (b : k → Matrix (y × x) (y × x) ℂ) : ℝ :=
+  sInf {lam : ℝ | 0 ≤ lam ∧ lam ≤ 1 ∧ TesterCompatibleAt lam a b}
+
+/-- Separate noise POVMs make the two mixtures marginals of one joint POVM. -/
+def POVMCompatibleAt {z j k : Type} [Fintype z] [DecidableEq z]
+    [Fintype j] [Fintype k] (lam : ℝ)
+    (p : j → Matrix z z ℂ) (q : k → Matrix z z ℂ) : Prop :=
+  ∃ (u : j → Matrix z z ℂ) (v : k → Matrix z z ℂ)
+    (g : j × k → Matrix z z ℂ),
+    ((∀ a, (u a).PosSemidef) ∧ ∑ a, u a = 1) ∧
+    ((∀ b, (v b).PosSemidef) ∧ ∑ b, v b = 1) ∧
+    ((∀ ab, (g ab).PosSemidef) ∧ ∑ ab, g ab = 1) ∧
+      (∀ a, ∑ b, g (a, b) = (1 - lam) • p a + lam • u a) ∧
+      (∀ b, ∑ a, g (a, b) = (1 - lam) • q b + lam • v b)
+
+/-- Infimum of the POVM mixing parameters in the unit interval. -/
+def povmRobustness {z j k : Type} [Fintype z] [DecidableEq z]
+    [Fintype j] [Fintype k]
+    (p : j → Matrix z z ℂ) (q : k → Matrix z z ℂ) : ℝ :=
+  sInf {lam : ℝ | 0 ≤ lam ∧ lam ≤ 1 ∧ POVMCompatibleAt lam p q}

+/-- The canonical POVMs act on the output and the support of the common input state. -/
+def claim : Prop :=
+  ∀ (y x j k : Type) [Fintype y] [DecidableEq y] [Fintype x] [DecidableEq x]
+    [Fintype j] [DecidableEq j] [Fintype k] [DecidableEq k]
+    (ρ : Matrix x x ℂ) (m : j → Matrix y y ℂ) (n : k → Matrix y y ℂ),
+    IsDensity ρ → ((∀ a, (m a).PosSemidef) ∧ ∑ a, m a = 1) →
+    ((∀ b, (n b).PosSemidef) ∧ ∑ b, n b = 1) →
+      testerRobustness (fun a => Matrix.kronecker (m a) ρ)
+        (fun b => Matrix.kronecker (n b) ρ) =
+      povmRobustness (fun a => Matrix.kronecker (m a)
+        (1 : Matrix (Fin ρ.rank) (Fin ρ.rank) ℂ))
+        (fun b => Matrix.kronecker (n b) (1 : Matrix (Fin ρ.rank) (Fin ρ.rank) ℂ))

+private theorem kronecker_sum {y x j : Type} [Fintype j]
+    (m : j → Matrix y y ℂ) (ρ : Matrix x x ℂ) :
+    (∑ a, Matrix.kronecker (m a) ρ) = Matrix.kronecker (∑ a, m a) ρ := by
+  exact (map_sum ((Matrix.kroneckerBilinear (R := ℂ)).flip ρ) m Finset.univ).symm
+
+private theorem povm_tensor_tester {y x j : Type} [Fintype y] [DecidableEq y]
+    [Fintype x] [Fintype j] (ρ : Matrix x x ℂ) (hρ : IsDensity ρ)
+    (m : j → Matrix y y ℂ) (hm : (∀ a, (m a).PosSemidef) ∧ ∑ a, m a = 1) :
+    IsTester (fun a => Matrix.kronecker (m a) ρ) := by
+  refine ⟨fun a => (hm.1 a).kronecker hρ.1, ρ, hρ, ?_⟩
+  rw [kronecker_sum, hm.2]
+
+private theorem partialTraceRight_sum {y x j : Type} [Fintype x] [Fintype j]
+    (t : j → Matrix (y × x) (y × x) ℂ) :
+    partialTraceRight (∑ a, t a) = ∑ a, partialTraceRight (t a) := by
+  ext a b
+  rw [Matrix.sum_apply]
+  change (∑ c, (∑ u, t u) (a, c) (b, c)) = ∑ u, ∑ c, t u (a, c) (b, c)
+  simp only [Matrix.sum_apply]
+  exact Finset.sum_comm
+
+private theorem tester_partialTrace_povm {y x j : Type} [Fintype y] [DecidableEq y]
+    [Fintype x] [Fintype j] (t : j → Matrix (y × x) (y × x) ℂ)
+    (ht : IsTester t) : (∀ a, (partialTraceRight (t a)).PosSemidef) ∧
+      ∑ a, partialTraceRight (t a) = 1 := by
+  refine ⟨fun a => partialTraceRight_posSemidef (ht.1 a), ?_⟩
+  obtain ⟨σ, hσ, hs⟩ := ht.2
+  rw [← partialTraceRight_sum, hs, partialTraceRight_kronecker, hσ.2, one_smul]
+
+private theorem povm_to_tester_compatible {y x j k : Type}
+    [Fintype y] [DecidableEq y] [Fintype x] [Fintype j] [Fintype k]
+    (ρ : Matrix x x ℂ) (hρ : IsDensity ρ) (lam : ℝ)
+    (m : j → Matrix y y ℂ) (n : k → Matrix y y ℂ)
+    (h : POVMCompatibleAt lam m n) :
+    TesterCompatibleAt lam (fun a => Matrix.kronecker (m a) ρ)
+      (fun b => Matrix.kronecker (n b) ρ) := by
+  obtain ⟨u, v, g, hu, hv, hg, hgm, hgn⟩ := h
+  refine ⟨fun a => Matrix.kronecker (u a) ρ,
+    fun b => Matrix.kronecker (v b) ρ,
+    fun ab => Matrix.kronecker (g ab) ρ,
+    povm_tensor_tester ρ hρ u hu, povm_tensor_tester ρ hρ v hv,
+    povm_tensor_tester ρ hρ g hg, ?_, ?_⟩
+  · intro a
+    rw [kronecker_sum, hgm a]
+    change ((1 - lam) • m a + lam • u a) ⊗ₖ ρ =
+      (1 - lam) • (m a ⊗ₖ ρ) + lam • (u a ⊗ₖ ρ)
+    rw [Matrix.add_kronecker, Matrix.smul_kronecker, Matrix.smul_kronecker]
+  · intro b
+    rw [kronecker_sum, hgn b]
+    change ((1 - lam) • n b + lam • v b) ⊗ₖ ρ =
+      (1 - lam) • (n b ⊗ₖ ρ) + lam • (v b ⊗ₖ ρ)
+    rw [Matrix.add_kronecker, Matrix.smul_kronecker, Matrix.smul_kronecker]
+
+private theorem tester_to_povm_compatible {y x j k : Type}
+    [Fintype y] [DecidableEq y] [Fintype x] [Fintype j] [Fintype k]
+    (ρ : Matrix x x ℂ) (hρ : IsDensity ρ) (lam : ℝ)
+    (m : j → Matrix y y ℂ) (n : k → Matrix y y ℂ)
+    (h : TesterCompatibleAt lam (fun a => Matrix.kronecker (m a) ρ)
+      (fun b => Matrix.kronecker (n b) ρ)) : POVMCompatibleAt lam m n := by
+  obtain ⟨e, f, c, he, hf, hc, hcm, hcn⟩ := h
+  refine ⟨fun a => partialTraceRight (e a), fun b => partialTraceRight (f b),
+    fun ab => partialTraceRight (c ab), tester_partialTrace_povm e he,
+    tester_partialTrace_povm f hf, tester_partialTrace_povm c hc, ?_, ?_⟩
+  · intro a
+    rw [← partialTraceRight_sum, hcm a, partialTraceRight_add,
+      partialTraceRight_smul, partialTraceRight_smul,
+      partialTraceRight_kronecker, hρ.2, one_smul]
+  · intro b
+    rw [← partialTraceRight_sum, hcn b, partialTraceRight_add,
+      partialTraceRight_smul, partialTraceRight_smul,
+      partialTraceRight_kronecker, hρ.2, one_smul]
+
+private theorem povm_tensor_identity {y j : Type} [Finite y] [DecidableEq y]
+    [Fintype j] (r : ℕ) (m : j → Matrix y y ℂ) (hm : (∀ a, (m a).PosSemidef) ∧ ∑ a, m a = 1) :
+    (∀ a, (Matrix.kronecker (m a) (1 : Matrix (Fin r) (Fin r) ℂ)).PosSemidef) ∧
+      ∑ a, Matrix.kronecker (m a) (1 : Matrix (Fin r) (Fin r) ℂ) = 1 := by
+  refine ⟨fun a => (hm.1 a).kronecker (Matrix.PosSemidef.one), ?_⟩
+  rw [kronecker_sum, hm.2]
+  exact Matrix.one_kronecker_one
+
+private theorem povm_to_ancilla_compatible {y j k : Type} [Fintype y] [DecidableEq y]
+    [Fintype j] [Fintype k] (r : ℕ) (lam : ℝ)
+    (m : j → Matrix y y ℂ) (n : k → Matrix y y ℂ)
+    (h : POVMCompatibleAt lam m n) :
+    POVMCompatibleAt lam (fun a => Matrix.kronecker (m a)

+      (fun b => Matrix.kronecker (n b) (1 : Matrix (Fin r) (Fin r) ℂ)) := by
+  obtain ⟨u, v, g, hu, hv, hg, hgm, hgn⟩ := h
+  refine ⟨fun a => Matrix.kronecker (u a) (1 : Matrix (Fin r) (Fin r) ℂ),
+    fun b => Matrix.kronecker (v b) (1 : Matrix (Fin r) (Fin r) ℂ),
+    fun ab => Matrix.kronecker (g ab) (1 : Matrix (Fin r) (Fin r) ℂ),
+    povm_tensor_identity r u hu, povm_tensor_identity r v hv,
+    povm_tensor_identity r g hg, ?_, ?_⟩
+  · intro a
+    rw [kronecker_sum, hgm a]
+    change ((1 - lam) • m a + lam • u a) ⊗ₖ (1 : Matrix (Fin r) (Fin r) ℂ) =

+    rw [kronecker_sum, hgn b]
+    change ((1 - lam) • n b + lam • v b) ⊗ₖ (1 : Matrix (Fin r) (Fin r) ℂ) =
+      (1 - lam) • (n b ⊗ₖ (1 : Matrix (Fin r) (Fin r) ℂ)) +
+        lam • (v b ⊗ₖ (1 : Matrix (Fin r) (Fin r) ℂ))
+    rw [Matrix.add_kronecker, Matrix.smul_kronecker, Matrix.smul_kronecker]
+
+private theorem compression_povm {y j : Type} [DecidableEq y]
+    [Fintype j] (r : ℕ) (hr : 0 < r)
+    (m : j → Matrix (y × Fin r) (y × Fin r) ℂ) (hm : (∀ a, (m a).PosSemidef) ∧ ∑ a, m a = 1) :
+    (∀ a, ((m a).submatrix (fun b => (b, ⟨0, hr⟩))
+      (fun b => (b, ⟨0, hr⟩))).PosSemidef) ∧

+    _ = (∑ a, m a).submatrix (fun b => (b, ⟨0, hr⟩))

+      simp only [Matrix.sum_apply, Matrix.submatrix_apply]

+      (fun b => (b, ⟨0, hr⟩)),
+    fun a => (g a).submatrix (fun b => (b, ⟨0, hr⟩))
+      (fun b => (b, ⟨0, hr⟩)),

+  · intro a
+    ext b d
+    have he := congrArg (fun z : Matrix (y × Fin r) (y × Fin r) ℂ =>

+    simpa only [Matrix.sum_apply, Matrix.submatrix_apply, Matrix.add_apply,
+      Matrix.smul_apply, hk] using he
+  · intro a
+    ext b d
+    have he := congrArg (fun z : Matrix (y × Fin r) (y × Fin r) ℂ =>
+      z (b, ⟨0, hr⟩) (d, ⟨0, hr⟩)) (hgn a)
+    simpa only [Matrix.sum_apply, Matrix.submatrix_apply, Matrix.add_apply,
+      Matrix.smul_apply, hk] using he

+theorem rank_pos_of_trace_one {a : Type*} [Fintype a] [DecidableEq a]
+    {A : Matrix a a ℂ} (htr : A.trace = 1) : 0 < A.rank := by
+  by_contra hn
+  have hz : A.rank = 0 := Nat.eq_zero_of_not_pos hn
+  have hrange : LinearMap.range A.mulVecLin = ⊥ := by
+    exact Submodule.finrank_eq_zero.mp hz
+  have hlin : A.mulVecLin = 0 := LinearMap.range_eq_bot.mp hrange
+  have hA : A = 0 := by
+    apply Matrix.toLin'.injective
+    simpa only [Matrix.toLin'_apply', Matrix.mulVecLin_zero] using hlin
+  simp [hA] at htr

+private theorem tester_feasible_eq {y x j k : Type}
+    [Fintype y] [DecidableEq y] [Fintype x] [Fintype j] [Fintype k]
+    (ρ : Matrix x x ℂ) (hρ : IsDensity ρ)
+    (m : j → Matrix y y ℂ) (n : k → Matrix y y ℂ) :
+    {lam : ℝ | 0 ≤ lam ∧ lam ≤ 1 ∧ TesterCompatibleAt lam
+      (fun a => Matrix.kronecker (m a) ρ) (fun b => Matrix.kronecker (n b) ρ)} =
+    {lam : ℝ | 0 ≤ lam ∧ lam ≤ 1 ∧ POVMCompatibleAt lam m n} := by
+  ext lam
+  exact and_congr_right fun _ => and_congr_right fun _ =>
+    ⟨tester_to_povm_compatible ρ hρ lam m n, povm_to_tester_compatible ρ hρ lam m n⟩
+
+private theorem ancilla_feasible_eq {y j k : Type} [Fintype y] [DecidableEq y]
+    [Fintype j] [Fintype k] (r : ℕ) (hr : 0 < r)
+    (m : j → Matrix y y ℂ) (n : k → Matrix y y ℂ) :
+    {lam : ℝ | 0 ≤ lam ∧ lam ≤ 1 ∧ POVMCompatibleAt lam m n} =
+    {lam : ℝ | 0 ≤ lam ∧ lam ≤ 1 ∧ POVMCompatibleAt lam
+      (fun a => Matrix.kronecker (m a) (1 : Matrix (Fin r) (Fin r) ℂ))
+      (fun b => Matrix.kronecker (n b) (1 : Matrix (Fin r) (Fin r) ℂ))} := by
+  ext lam
+  exact and_congr_right fun _ => and_congr_right fun _ =>
+    ⟨povm_to_ancilla_compatible r lam m n, ancilla_to_povm_compatible r hr lam m n⟩
+
+/-- Tester and canonical measurement robustness agree for a common ancilla-free state. -/
+theorem result : claim := by
+  intro y x j k _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ ρ m n hρ _hm _hn
+  change sInf _ = sInf _
+  exact congrArg sInf ((tester_feasible_eq ρ hρ m n).trans
+    (ancilla_feasible_eq ρ.rank (rank_pos_of_trace_one hρ.2) m n))
+
+end D5.S3.Quantum.QuantumChannels.AncillaFreeTesterRobustnessEquality

+# Ancilla-free testers with a common normalization state have canonical POVM robustness
+
+## Problem
+
+M. Sedlák, D. Reitzner, G. Chiribella and M. Ziman, *Incompatible measurements on quantum causal networks*, Phys. Rev. A 93, 052323 (2016), arXiv:1511.00976v2, Section VI.C, ask (verbatim from `ti_pra_07.tex`, line 807, retaining the source's TeX macros):
+
+> It is an open question whether  the equality $\Rt({\st A},  {\st B})  =  \Rm(  \st P,  \st Q )$ holds for all ancilla-free testers.
+
+Here $R_{\rm t}$ and $R_{\rm m}$ denote tester and measurement robustness. Section VI restricts attention to testers with the same normalization state (`ti_pra_07.tex`, lines 758 and 772); that hypothesis is retained. Proposition 3 characterizes ancilla-free testers as $T_a=M_a\otimes\rho$ for an output POVM $M$ and an input density matrix $\rho$ (lines 333–338). Definitions and locators are in [the literature note](../Library/Observer/sedlakreitznerchiribellaziman2016testers.md).
+
+Issue [#23653](https://github.com/the-omega-institute/trureturing/issues/23653) fixes the following finite-dimensional reading. Let $y,x,j,k$ be finite types with decidable equality, indexing output coordinates, input coordinates and the two outcome sets. Let $\rho$ be a complex matrix on $x$ with $\rho\succeq0$ and $\operatorname{Tr}\rho=1$. Let $M=(M_a)_{a\in j}$ and $N=(N_b)_{b\in k}$ be complex output POVMs: each effect is positive semidefinite and each family sums to $I_y$. With $r=\operatorname{rank}\rho$, the statement is
+
+$$
+R_{\rm t}\bigl((M_a\otimes\rho)_a,(N_b\otimes\rho)_b\bigr)
+=R_{\rm m}\bigl((M_a\otimes I_r)_a,(N_b\otimes I_r)_b\bigr).
+$$
+
+In the module, `IsTester` means positive semidefinite effects summing to $I_y\otimes\sigma$ for some positive semidefinite $\sigma$ of trace one. `TesterCompatibleAt` at a real $\lambda$ requires noise testers $E,F$ and a joint tester $C$ with
+
+$$
+\sum_b C_{ab}=(1-\lambda)A_a+\lambda E_a,
+\qquad
+\sum_a C_{ab}=(1-\lambda)B_b+\lambda F_b.
+$$
+
+The noises have separate existential witnesses; their normalization states are not prescribed to equal $\rho$, and their effects need not be products. `POVMCompatibleAt` uses the same marginal equations with noise POVMs and a joint POVM, each positive semidefinite and summing to the identity. `testerRobustness` and `povmRobustness` are the real infima of their respective feasible $\lambda\in[0,1]$. The source uses minima; attainment is not part of `claim` or `result`. The displayed equality, with these infimum definitions and $I_r$ indexed by `Fin ρ.rank`, is proved.
+
+## Motivation
+
+For a common normalization state, the question isolates incompatibility arising from the measurements. Proposition 15 gives an upper bound by canonical POVM robustness, and Proposition 16 gives equality for a common pure normalization state (`ti_pra_07.tex`, lines 776–805). The question asks whether mixed normalization states also give equality throughout the ancilla-free class. Its resolution determines whether allowing arbitrary tester noise can reduce the required mixing parameter below that of the associated output measurements.
